## Setup

### Create Objects

* Clone the GitHub repository.
* In Snowsight, on the left hand navigation menu, select **Projects** >> **Workspaces**, click on **+ Add new** >> **SQL File**, and copy the contents of setup.sql into it.
* Execute all statements in order from top to bottom.

The script runs as **ACCOUNTADMIN** and creates:

* The **DASH\_MCP\_DB.DATA** schema with financial services tables loaded from AWS S3, and the **DASH\_WH\_S** warehouse
* The **SEND\_EMAIL** stored procedure and **EMAIL\_INTEGRATION** notification integration, used later as a custom tool
* The **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE** role, granted to you. MCP clients use this least-privileged role instead of ACCOUNTADMIN.

> NOTE: If Cortex Analyst models aren't available in your region, uncomment the `ALTER ACCOUNT SET CORTEX_ENABLED_CROSS_REGION` statement near the top of the script to enable cross-region inference.

### Cortex Search Service

This tool lets an agent search and retrieve information from unstructured text, such as customer support tickets, Slack conversations, or contracts. It uses Cortex Search to index and query the text, enabling Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).

* In Snowsight, on the left hand navigation menu, select **AI & ML** >> **Cortex Search** and click on **Create**

  + Role and Warehouse: **ACCOUNTADMIN** | **DASH\_WH\_S**
  + Database and Schema: **DASH\_MCP\_DB.DATA**
  + Name: **SUPPORT\_TICKETS**
* Click on **Next** and complete the remaining steps:

  + Select data to be indexed: **Table or view** >> **FACT\_SUPPORT\_TICKETS**
  + Columns to include in the search results: select all
  + Search column: **DESCRIPTION**
  + Attribute (filter) columns: **CATEGORY**, **SUBCATEGORY**, **PRIORITY**, **CHANNEL**, **STATUS**, **SATISFACTION\_SCORE**
  + Target lag: keep the default, then click on **Create**

> NOTE: Enter the name in uppercase. Snowsight double-quotes service names, so a mixed-case name such as `Support_Tickets` becomes case-sensitive and won't match the `DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.SUPPORT_TICKETS` identifier used in the MCP server specification.

### Cortex Analyst Semantic View

This tool lets an agent query structured data by generating SQL. It relies on a semantic view, which maps business concepts (for example, "customer lifetime value" or "risk profile") to the underlying tables and columns. The Snowflake-managed MCP server supports semantic views only, not legacy semantic model YAML files on a stage.

* Download FINANCIAL\_SERVICES\_ANALYTICS.yaml from the repository you cloned.
* In Snowsight, on the left hand navigation menu, select **Projects** >> **Workspaces** and click on **+ Add new** >> **Semantic View**. This opens Semantic View Autopilot.

  + Location: **DASH\_MCP\_DB.DATA**
  + Name: **FINANCIAL\_SERVICES\_ANALYTICS**
* When Autopilot asks for context, choose to upload a YAML specification and select **FINANCIAL\_SERVICES\_ANALYTICS.yaml**. Autopilot converts it into a semantic view.
* Save the semantic view.

### Grant Access to the Tools

Run the following in your SQL file so that **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE** can use the search service and semantic view.

```
```
USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN;

GRANT USAGE ON CORTEX SEARCH SERVICE DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.SUPPORT_TICKETS TO ROLE DASH_MCP_ROLE;
GRANT SELECT ON SEMANTIC VIEW DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.FINANCIAL_SERVICES_ANALYTICS TO ROLE DASH_MCP_ROLE;
```
```

> NOTE: Access to an MCP server doesn't grant access to its tools. The role an MCP client uses needs a privilege on each underlying object: USAGE on Cortex Search services, agents, functions, and procedures, and SELECT on semantic views.

## Snowflake MCP Server

> PREREQUISITE: Successful completion of steps outlined under **Setup**.

### Create the MCP Server

Run the following in the same SQL file to create the MCP server and grant **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE** access to it.

```
```
USE ROLE ACCOUNTADMIN;
USE SCHEMA DASH_MCP_DB.DATA;

CREATE OR REPLACE MCP SERVER DASH_MCP_SERVER FROM SPECIFICATION
$$
tools:
  - name: "Finance_and_Risk_Assessment_Semantic_View"
    identifier: "DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.FINANCIAL_SERVICES_ANALYTICS"
    type: "CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE"
    description: "Comprehensive semantic model for financial services analytics, providing unified business definitions and relationships across customer data, transactions, marketing campaigns, support interactions, and risk assessments."
    title: "Financial And Risk Assessment"
  - name: "Support_Tickets_Cortex_Search"
    identifier: "DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.SUPPORT_TICKETS"
    type: "CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY"
    description: "A tool that performs keyword and vector search over unstructured support tickets data."
    title: "Support Tickets Cortex Search"
  - name: "SQL_Execution_Tool"
    type: "SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL"
    description: "A tool to execute read-only SQL queries against the connected Snowflake database."
    title: "SQL Execution Tool"
    config:
      read_only: true
      warehouse: "DASH_WH_S"
  - name: "Send_Email"
    identifier: "DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.SEND_EMAIL"
    type: "GENERIC"
    description: "A custom tool to send emails to the user's verified email address."
    title: "Send_Email"
    config:
      type: "procedure"
      warehouse: "DASH_WH_S"
      input_schema:
        type: "object"
        properties:
          body:
            description: "Use HTML-Syntax for this. If the content you get is in markdown, translate it to HTML. If body is not provided, summarize the last question and use that as content for the email."
            type: "string"
          recipient_email:
            description: "If the email is not provided, send it to the current user's email address."
            type: "string"
          subject:
            description: "If subject is not provided, use Snowflake MCP Server."
            type: "string"
$$;

GRANT USAGE ON MCP SERVER DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.DASH_MCP_SERVER TO ROLE DASH_MCP_ROLE;
```
```

The server exposes four tools:

* **Finance\_and\_Risk\_Assessment\_Semantic\_View** (Cortex Analyst): turns a question into SQL over the semantic view. It returns the generated SQL, not the query results.
* **Support\_Tickets\_Cortex\_Search** (Cortex Search): searches support ticket descriptions.
* **SQL\_Execution\_Tool**: runs read-only SQL, such as the SQL that Cortex Analyst generates.
* **Send\_Email** (custom tool): calls the **SEND\_EMAIL** stored procedure.

### Create a Programmatic Access Token

MCP clients authenticate with a programmatic access token (PAT) or OAuth. This guide uses a PAT because every client and `curl` support it. Restrict the token to **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE** so that clients never run with ACCOUNTADMIN privileges.

* In Snowsight, on the left hand navigation menu, select **Governance & security** >> **Users & roles** and select your user.
* Under **Programmatic access tokens**, click on **Generate new token**.

  + Name: **MCP\_GUIDE\_TOKEN**
  + Expires in: choose a short expiration, such as 7 days
  + Select **One specific role (recommended)** and choose **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE**
* Click on **Generate**, then copy the token and store it somewhere safe. You can't view it again after you close the dialog.

> NOTE: A PAT for a person user only works if the user is subject to a network policy. If your account or user has no network policy, select **Bypass requirement for network policy** in the dialog for a temporary bypass, or ask your administrator to add one.

You can also generate the token with SQL:

```
```
ALTER USER ADD PROGRAMMATIC ACCESS TOKEN MCP_GUIDE_TOKEN
  ROLE_RESTRICTION = 'DASH_MCP_ROLE'
  DAYS_TO_EXPIRY = 7;
```
```

> NOTE: For production, Snowflake recommends OAuth instead of hardcoded tokens. Most hosted clients, such as Claude and ChatGPT, connect with OAuth.

### Find Your MCP Server URL

Every MCP client connects to the same URL:

```
```
https://<YOUR-ACCOUNT-URL>/api/v2/databases/DASH_MCP_DB/schemas/DATA/mcp-servers/DASH_MCP_SERVER
```
```

To get your account hostname, run:

```
```
SELECT REPLACE(LOWER(CURRENT_ORGANIZATION_NAME() || '-' || CURRENT_ACCOUNT_NAME()), '_', '-') || '.snowflakecomputing.com' AS account_url;
```
```

> NOTE: Use hyphens (-), not underscores (\_), in the hostname. MCP clients fail to connect, often with a TLS certificate error, when the hostname contains underscores.

### Verify with curl

Before you configure a client, list the server's tools with `curl`. Replace  and  with your values.

```
```
curl -X POST "https://<YOUR-ACCOUNT-URL>/api/v2/databases/DASH_MCP_DB/schemas/DATA/mcp-servers/DASH_MCP_SERVER" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-PAT>" \
  --data '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 1,
    "method": "tools/list",
    "params": {}
  }'
```
```

**What to expect:** A JSON response that lists the four tools by name (`Finance_and_Risk_Assessment_Semantic_View`, `Support_Tickets_Cortex_Search`, `SQL_Execution_Tool`, and `Send_Email`), each with an `inputSchema`. For example, the Cortex Analyst tool takes a `message`, the search tool takes a `query` plus optional `columns`, `filter`, and `limit`, and the SQL tool takes `sql`. If you get an error instead, check the account URL, the PAT, and the network policy note above.

Then call a tool. This example asks the SQL tool to count customers:

```
```
curl -X POST "https://<YOUR-ACCOUNT-URL>/api/v2/databases/DASH_MCP_DB/schemas/DATA/mcp-servers/DASH_MCP_SERVER" \
  --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR-PAT>" \
  --data '{
    "jsonrpc": "2.0",
    "id": 2,
    "method": "tools/call",
    "params": {
      "name": "SQL_Execution_Tool",
      "arguments": { "sql": "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM DASH_MCP_DB.DATA.DIM_CUSTOMERS" }
    }
  }'
```
```

**What to expect:** A result whose `content` contains the query output, a count of 5,000 customers. Tool calls can stream their response as Server-Sent Events, which is why the `Accept` header lists both `application/json` and `text/event-stream`. In that case the JSON arrives in a `data:` line.

* **Role:** the PAT is restricted to **DASH\_MCP\_ROLE**, so the client sees only the objects that role can use

Add the server using your client's MCP settings. Most clients use a JSON configuration with a `url` and `headers`, similar to the example below. For step-by-step instructions for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and other clients, see Connect from common MCP clients.

## Ask Questions

Once your client lists the Snowflake tools, start a new chat and ask the following questions. Answers are generated live, so wording and formatting vary by client and model. Your client's model decides which tool to call, so the notes below describe what to look for.

### Q1. *What is the average customer lifetime value by region for customers with Low risk profile?*

**What to expect:** The client calls the Cortex Analyst tool, which returns the SQL it generated, then runs that SQL with the SQL tool. You should see five regions with similar averages of roughly $48,000 to $52,500, with Central the highest and East the lowest.

### Q2. *Show me the risk profile distribution across customer segments with transaction volumes. Include the number of customers, transaction counts, and average transactions per customer for each segment and risk profile combination.*

**What to expect:** The same Cortex Analyst plus SQL pattern, returning a table with 12 rows, one for each combination of the four customer segments (Basic, Standard, Premium, and VIP) and three risk profiles (Low, Medium, and High). Each customer averages roughly 9 to 11 transactions.

### Q3. *Can you summarize the overall sentiment based on the support tickets?*

**What to expect:** The client calls the Cortex Search tool, then summarizes the tickets it retrieves. Many tickets are routine questions about rates, fees, and accounts.

### Q4. *Which support categories would benefit most from automated responses based on ticket analysis?*

**What to expect:** Depending on your client, it searches the tickets, queries **FACT\_SUPPORT\_TICKETS** with SQL, or both. The categories have similar ticket volumes, so expect the answer to focus on routine categories, such as rate questions, general questions, and fee inquiries, and on response times and satisfaction scores.

### Custom Tools

Custom tools let you expose your own functions and stored procedures through the MCP server with `type: "GENERIC"` in the specification. The **Send\_Email** tool calls the **SEND\_EMAIL** stored procedure, which sends email through the **EMAIL\_INTEGRATION** notification integration.

Enter the following prompt, replacing **YOUR-EMAIL-ADDRESS** with your verified email address:

#### *Send me an email with a summary of the analysis to YOUR-EMAIL-ADDRESS.*

**What to expect:** The client calls the **Send\_Email** tool, which returns `Email sent successfully`. Check your inbox for the summary. Snowflake only sends email to verified addresses.

# CREATE MCP SERVER¶

Creates a new MCP (Model Context Protocol) server or replaces an existing MCP server.

**See also:**

## Syntax¶

```
CREATE [ OR REPLACE ] MCP SERVER [ IF NOT EXISTS ] <name>
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$<specification_yaml>$$
```

## Parameters¶

**`name`**:   String that specifies the identifier for the MCP server; must be unique for the schema in which the MCP server is created.

    In addition, the identifier must start with an alphabetic character and cannot contain spaces or special characters unless the
    entire identifier string is enclosed in double quotes (for example, `"My object"`). Identifiers enclosed in double quotes are also
    case-sensitive.

    For more information, see Identifier requirements.
**`FROM SPECIFICATION $$specification_yaml$$`**:   Specifies the YAML specification defining the tools and configuration for the MCP server.

    The specification must include a `tools` array with one or more tool definitions, a `tool_config` entry, or both. Each tool in `tools` must specify:

    * `name`: Unique identifier for the tool
    * `type`: Tool type (see supported tool types)
    * `title`: Human-readable title for the tool
    * `description`: Description of what the tool does

    For `GENERIC` and `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN` tools, you can also specify an optional `annotations` object with MCP tool behavior hints:

    * `readOnlyHint`: If `true`, the tool doesn’t modify its environment.
    * `destructiveHint`: If `true`, the tool might perform destructive updates. This hint is meaningful only when `readOnlyHint` is `false`.
    * `idempotentHint`: If `true`, repeated calls with the same arguments have the same effect as one call.
    * `openWorldHint`: If `true`, the tool might interact with external entities.

    Each annotation is optional. For omitted annotations, Snowflake uses the default for the tool type. The defaults for `GENERIC` and `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN` are `readOnlyHint: false`, `destructiveHint: true`, `idempotentHint: false`, and `openWorldHint: true`.

    Tool annotations are hints for MCP clients. They don’t enforce tool behavior or replace access control. Configure privileges for the underlying object according to the actual operations that the tool can perform.

    **Supported tool types:**

    * `CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY`: Cortex Search Service tool
    * `CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE`: Cortex Analyst tool
    * `SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL`: SQL execution tool
    * `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN`: Cortex Agent tool
    * `CODING_AGENT`: Coding Agent tool, with no stored agent object. Snowflake adds the `code_toolset_all` tool on every run
    * `GENERIC`: Custom tool for UDFs and stored procedures

    **Tool-specific requirements:**

    For `CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY`, `CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE`, and `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN` tools:

    * `identifier`: Fully qualified name of the underlying object (for example, `database.schema.object_name`)

    If an MCP server has at least one of the `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN` or `CODING_AGENT` tools, Snowflake automatically adds three tools: `ASYNC_AGENT_RUN_STATUS`, `AGENT_RUN_RESULT`, and `ASYNC_AGENT_RUN_CANCEL`. If `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN` or `CODING_AGENT` is invoked with `"background": true`, it returns immediately with a handle; that handle can be passed to `ASYNC_AGENT_RUN_STATUS` or `ASYNC_AGENT_RUN_CANCEL` to get the status or cancel a run respectively. `AGENT_RUN_RESULT` can be used to fetch a result from a run (whether background or not). See Cortex Agent supplementary tools and Run an agent tool in the background.

    For `GENERIC` tools:

    * `identifier`: Fully qualified name of the UDF or stored procedure
    * `config`: Configuration object specifying:
      + `type`: Either `function` (for UDF) or `procedure` (for stored procedure)
      + `warehouse`: Warehouse to use for execution
      + `input_schema`: JSON schema defining the function/procedure parameters

    For `CODING_AGENT` tools:

    * Add the tool to the server specification. Omit `identifier`. This tool does not reference a stored agent object.
    * `config`: Optional agent configuration. It can include any field of the Cortex Agents run request, such as `model`, `instructions`, `tools`, `tool_resources`, and `skills`. See Coding Agent.
    * Snowflake appends `code_toolset_all` after any tools in `config`. A run can include `code_toolset_all` or `code_execution`, but not both. The appended tool defaults to `always_ask`, so a state-modifying tool pauses and the call ends before it runs. Set `tool_resources.code_toolset_all.permission_policy.type` to `always_allow` for a trusted automation that should run those tools in one call. See Coding Agent.

    **Generated agent tools:**

    To serve every Cortex Agent that the caller’s role can use, add a top-level `tool_config` list with one entry:

    * `type`: `CORTEX_AGENT_RUN`
    * `selection`: `all`

    The entry accepts no other keys, and the list accepts only one entry. Snowflake doesn’t store the generated tools in the specification. It generates them on each `tools/list` request, for the role that makes the request. See Serve every agent the caller can use.

## Access control requirements¶

A role used to execute this operation must have the following
privileges at a minimum:

| Privilege | Object |
| --- | --- |
| CREATE MCP SERVER | Schema |
| USAGE | Schema |

For tools that reference other objects, additional privileges are required:

| Privilege | Object |
| --- | --- |
| USAGE | Cortex Search Service (for CORTEX\_SEARCH\_SERVICE\_QUERY tools) |
| SELECT | Semantic View (for CORTEX\_ANALYST\_MESSAGE tools) |
| USAGE | Cortex Agent (for CORTEX\_AGENT\_RUN tools) |
| USAGE | User-defined function or stored procedure (for GENERIC tools) |
| USAGE | Warehouse (for GENERIC tools) |

Operating on an object in a schema requires at least one privilege on the parent database and at least one privilege on the parent schema.

For instructions on creating a custom role with a specified set of privileges, see Creating custom roles.

For general information about roles and privilege grants for performing SQL actions on
securable objects, see Overview of Access Control.

## Usage notes¶

* The OR REPLACE and IF NOT EXISTS clauses are mutually exclusive. They can’t both be used in the same statement.
* CREATE OR REPLACE *<object>* statements are atomic. That is, when an object is replaced, the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.

* CREATE OR REPLACE *<object>* statements are atomic. That is, when an object is replaced, the old object is deleted and the new object is created in a single transaction.
* When configuring hostnames for MCP server connections, use hyphens (`-`) instead of underscores (`_`). MCP servers have connection issues with hostnames containing underscores.
* External OAuth authorization-server binding and advertised scopes aren’t set in the MCP server specification. Configure them with the `OAUTH_AUTHORIZATION_SERVER` and `OAUTH_SCOPES_SUPPORTED` parameters on the enclosing account, database, or schema. For details, see Configure External OAuth authentication for MCP servers.
* The MCP server specification is stored as metadata and can be viewed using DESCRIBE MCP SERVER.
* Multiple tools can be defined in a single MCP server specification.
* Tool names must be unique within a single MCP server.
* If the specification has a `tool_config` entry, tool names in `tools` can’t start with `sf_`. Snowflake reserves this prefix for generated agent tools.
* `DESCRIBE MCP SERVER` and `GET_DDL` show the `tool_config` entry, but not the tools that Snowflake generates from it.
* Regarding metadata:

  Attention

  Customers should ensure that no personal data (other than for a User object), sensitive data, export-controlled data, or other regulated data is entered as metadata when using the Snowflake service. For more information, see Metadata fields in Snowflake.

## Examples¶

**Example 1: Create MCP server with Cortex Search and Analyst tools**

```
CREATE MCP SERVER my_mcp_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - name: "product-search"
        type: "CORTEX_SEARCH_SERVICE_QUERY"
        identifier: "database1.schema1.cortex_search_service1"
        description: "Cortex search service for all products"
        title: "Product Search"

      - name: "revenue-semantic-view"
        type: "CORTEX_ANALYST_MESSAGE"
        identifier: "database1.schema1.semantic_view_1"
        description: "Semantic view for all revenue tables"
        title: "Semantic view for revenue"
  $$;
```

**Example 2: Create MCP server with SQL execution tool**

```
CREATE MCP SERVER sql_exec_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "SQL Execution Tool"
        name: "sql_exec_tool"
        type: "SYSTEM_EXECUTE_SQL"
        description: "A tool to execute SQL queries against the connected Snowflake database."
  $$;
```

**Example 3: Create MCP server with custom UDF tool**

```
CREATE MCP SERVER custom_tools_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "Multiply by Ten"
        identifier: "example_database.agents.multiply_by_ten"
        name: "multiply_by_ten"
        type: "GENERIC"
        description: "Multiplies input value by ten and returns the result."
        config:
          type: "function"
          warehouse: "compute_service_warehouse"
          input_schema:
            type: "object"
            properties:
              x:
                description: "A number to be multiplied by ten"
                type: "number"
  $$;
```

**Example 4: Create MCP server with custom stored procedure tool**

```
CREATE MCP SERVER procedure_tools_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "Calculate Values"
        identifier: "example_database.agents.calculate_values_sp"
        name: "calculate_values_sp"
        type: "GENERIC"
        description: "Calculates the product and sum of two numbers and returns them in a JSON object."
        annotations:
          readOnlyHint: true
          destructiveHint: false
          idempotentHint: true
          openWorldHint: false
        config:
          type: "procedure"
          warehouse: "compute_service_warehouse"
          input_schema:
            type: "object"
            properties:
              x:
                description: "First number"
                type: "number"
              y:
                description: "Second number"
                type: "number"
  $$;
```

**Example 5: Create MCP server with Agent tool**

```
CREATE MCP SERVER agent_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "Customer Service Agent"
        name: "customer_agent"
        type: "CORTEX_AGENT_RUN"
        identifier: "support_db.agents_schema.customer_service_agent"
        description: "Agent that handles customer service inquiries"
        annotations:
          openWorldHint: false
  $$;
```

**Example 6: Create MCP server with a coding agent tool**

Add a `CODING_AGENT` tool to the server specification. Clients call the tool with a `text` argument. A later call passes the returned `thread_id` and `message_id` as `thread_id` and `parent_message_id`. `parent_message_id` is required whenever `thread_id` is set. Pass `"0"` to start a new branch at the thread root.

```
CREATE MCP SERVER coding_agent_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "Coding agent"
        name: "ask_coding_agent"
        type: "CODING_AGENT"
        description: "Ask the coding agent. code_toolset_all gives the agent a managed sandbox where it can write and run code. That sandbox stays attached to the conversation thread."
        config:
          model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"
          instructions:
            response: "Write and run code when that answers the question."
          tool_resources:
            code_toolset_all:
              permission_policy:
                type: always_allow
  $$;
```

**Example 7: Create MCP server that serves every agent the caller can use**

After the explicit `revenue_agent` tool, the server lists a generated tool for each Cortex Agent that the caller’s role has the USAGE privilege on, within the generated tool limits. Snowflake doesn’t generate a second tool for `revenue_agent`.

```
CREATE MCP SERVER all_agents_server
  FROM SPECIFICATION $$
    tools:
      - title: "Revenue Agent"
        name: "revenue_agent"
        type: "CORTEX_AGENT_RUN"
        identifier: "sales_db.agents.revenue_agent"
        description: "Answers revenue questions"
    tool_config:
      - type: "CORTEX_AGENT_RUN"
        selection: "all"
  $$;
```
